rules.title: Daily steps

evidence.cite: Paluch et al., Lancet Public Health 2022
evidence.claim: Benefit keeps rising to 8–10k steps/day under 60. Top quarter (~11k) had about half the mortality of the bottom (~3.5k).

messages: {value} steps and it's {time}. Pace says {expected}. Your chair is filing for overtime.
{value} steps. Target {target}. That's {remaining} to go — get up, soldier.
{time} check: {value} steps. People who walk 8k+ a day die later. Move.

rules.title: Weekly exercise

evidence.claim: Nearly all the mortality benefit comes at 150–300 vigorous or 300–600 moderate minutes a week.

messages: {value} exercise minutes this week. The floor is {target}. You're behind and the week is not.
Weekly exercise: {value}/{target} min. {remaining} minutes short. Lace up.
{value} minutes of exercise since Monday. The research wants {target}. Embarrassing. Fix it.

rules.title: Strength training

evidence.cite: Momma et al., Br J Sports Med 2022
evidence.claim: 30–60 min/week of muscle-strengthening is linked to 10–20% lower mortality — more when combined with cardio.

messages: {value} minutes of strength training this week. Target {target}. Those weights aren't going to lift themselves.
Strength: {value}/{target} min. Muscle is a longevity organ. Go use it.
Zero excuses, {value} minutes of lifting. Get {remaining} more before Sunday.

rules.title: Sleep

evidence.cite: Windred et al., SLEEP 2024; Yin et al., JAHA 2017
evidence.claim: Regular sleep timing predicted mortality as well as duration (20–48% lower risk); risk is lowest around 7 hours.

messages_short: {value} of sleep. Minimum is 7 hours. Whatever you were doing at midnight wasn't worth it.
You slept {value}. The research says 7+. Bed earlier tonight — that's an order.
messages_irregular: Bedtime was {shift} off your usual. Regular sleepers live longer. Pick a time and stick to it.
Your bedtime wandered {shift} from normal. Consistency beats heroics. Same time tonight.

evidence.claim: Each extra 10 bpm of resting heart rate is linked to ~9% higher all-cause mortality.

evidence.cite: Kodama et al., JAMA 2009; Mandsager et al., JAMA Netw Open 2018
evidence.claim: The strongest single predictor: each +1 MET (3.5 ml/kg/min) ≈ 13% lower mortality, with no plateau. Apple Watch reads ~6 low, so watch the trend.
